coach_says: Your biggest gap is aerobic-high (tempo/threshold) work, while anaerobic load is already over target — so this week trades punchy efforts for sustained climbing and tempo blocks on Tuesday AM and Friday. With HRV unbalanced and readiness at 54, Tuesday's non-negotiable double is your one true hard day, buffered by an easy Monday gym session and a mandatory easy Wednesday. Watch morning HRV after Tuesday — if it stays unbalanced into Friday, drop the tempo blocks and ride the long route at pure Zone 2.

days.details: Warm-up: 8 min easy bike + dynamic hip openers and leg swings. Romanian Deadlift 3x8 (moderate load, RPE 7), Single-Leg Glute Bridge 3x10/side, Seated Cable Row 3x10, Pallof Press 3x10/side, Side Plank 3x30s/side, Bird Dog 2x8/side. Rest 90s between sets. Objective: posterior chain, hip stability and trunk strength with deliberately no heavy quad-dominant loading — legs stay fresh for tomorrow's double hard day. Wet forecast, so lunch gym is the right call.

days.session: Double day: AM hills + PM hard MTB group ride
days.details: AM Hills road ride (~60 min, committed): 15 min warm-up Z2, then 3x8 min sustained seated climbing at Z3–low Z4 (tempo/threshold, NOT sprints — your anaerobic load is already over target, your aerobic-high is the gap), 4 min easy spin between efforts, 10 min cool-down. Light drizzle only — rideable. PM Hard MTB group ride (~90 min, non-negotiable): ride as the group dictates, but avoid stacking extra sprints beyond what the ride demands. Fuel well between sessions and prioritise an early night.

40 min gentle recovery flow indoors: hip openers (pigeon, lizard), hamstring work (forward folds), thoracic mobility, 5 min breathing/relaxation to finish. Heavy showers and 35 km/h winds make outdoors a non-starter anyway. Strictly easy — this day exists to absorb Tuesday's double. No efforts of any kind.

Warmup: 200m easy mixed stroke. Main set: 4x100m steady aerobic (RPE 5-6, conversational-effort equivalent) with 20s rest; 4x50m drill/swim by 25 (catch-up or fist drill) with 15s rest; 2x100m smooth steady with 20s rest. Cooldown: 100m very easy. Total: 1100m. Objective: low-impact aerobic maintenance and recovery flush between Tuesday's double and Friday's quality ride. Showers forecast — pool is ideal.

2.5 hr outdoor road ride — Friday is one of your two dry windows, use it. Primary objective: close the aerobic-high shortage. Structure: 30 min Z2 warm-up, then 2x20 min tempo at Z3 (RPE 6-7, sustained and controlled, cadence 85-95) with 10 min Z2 between blocks, remainder Z2 home. Ride the tempo blocks into the ~20 km/h headwind for steady resistance, cruise back with it. Checkpoint: if HRV is still unbalanced this morning or legs feel flat, drop the tempo blocks and ride the full duration at Z2.

Warm-up: 8 min easy bike + bodyweight squats and lunges. Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8/side (moderate load, RPE 7 — deliberately NOT heavy, long ride tomorrow), Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift 3x8/side, Lat Pulldown 3x8, Hip Thrust 3x10 (moderate), Standing Calf Raise 3x12, Front Plank 3x45s. Rest 90s between sets. Objective: single-leg strength, hip stability and upper-body pull — load capped so legs are fresh for Sunday's endurance ride. Showers forecast, so indoor lunch slot fits.

3 hr outdoor road ride in the best weather of the week — clear skies, moderate 20 km/h wind (head out into the wind, return with it). Primary objective: aerobic base volume. Zone 2 throughout (RPE 3-4, fully conversational), no intervals, cadence 85-95. Your aerobic-low load is healthy — this maintains it while keeping the week near 80/20 after Tuesday's double and Friday's tempo. Eat 60g carbs/hr from hour one, and finish feeling like you could ride another hour.
